links.comparator_used: Initial role-based prompt V1 used as baseline without refinement, compared with iteratively refined prompts V2 and V3 on 45 simulated dialogues rated by 4 gastroenterologists
links.outcome: Expert-rated dialogue quality across 6 dimensions (information gathering, judgment timing, recommendation accuracy, personalization and clarity, safety and fairness, actionability)
links.effect: Kruskal-Wallis P<.001 for all 6 dimensions; V3 scored higher than V1 on all dimensions (adjusted P<.05); median scores rose progressively from V1 to V3, with no decrease in mean scores on any dimension
links.quote: Post hoc analyses using Dunn test with Bonferroni correction showed that prompt V3 scored higher than prompt V1 across all dimensions (adjusted P <.05).

links.comparator_used: Prompt V2 (slot-filling with knowledge base, no output format, simplified language or empathetic style constraints) compared with V3, which added constrained output length and structure, simplified language and an empathetic style
links.outcome: Expert-rated personalization and clarity, and safety and fairness (plus the other 4 dimensions) in simulated dialogues
links.effect: V3 vs V2: personalization and clarity adjusted P=.02; safety and fairness adjusted P<.001; the remaining dimensions not significant (adjusted P>.05)
links.quote: Compared with prompt V2, prompt V3 demonstrated statistically significant improvements only in personalization and clarity (adjusted P =.02) and safety and fairness (adjusted P <.001), whereas differences in the remaining dimensions did not reach statistical significance (adjusted P >.05).
